security_audit.summary: The static alerts are false positives caused by Nuxt documentation examples in markdown files. I found no evidence of prompt injection, malicious command execution, credential exfiltration, or unauthorized network activity.

remediation.issue: Documentation examples include placeholders that resemble secrets and environment files.
remediation.suggestion: Label placeholders clearly and remind users to keep private runtime config server-only.

remediation.issue: The dev-server example shows binding to 0.0.0.0 for mobile testing.
remediation.suggestion: Add a warning to use this only on trusted networks and prefer localhost by default.

content.user_title: Build Nuxt Apps with Focused Guidance
content.value_statement: Nuxt projects involve many conventions across routing, data fetching, server APIs, and rendering modes. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused Nuxt guidance from curated reference files.
actual_capabilities: Explain Nuxt directory structure, file-based routing, layouts, middleware, and route validation.
Guide useFetch, useAsyncData, $fetch, caching, refresh, and SSR data patterns.
Describe runtime config, app config, environment variables, and module configuration.
Help plan server routes, server middleware, Nitro plugins, and deployment targets.
Compare universal rendering, client rendering, hybrid rendering, and route rules.
Explain modules, layers, hooks, auto-imported components, and composables.
limitations: The references target Nuxt 3.x and were generated on January 28, 2026.
It does not run Nuxt CLI commands or inspect a project unless the host tool does so.
It does not replace a security review for production server routes or authentication code.
It may not cover Nuxt changes released after the source snapshot.

use_cases.title: Build Nuxt Pages
use_cases.description: Create pages, layouts, route middleware, and navigation patterns that match Nuxt conventions.

use_cases.title: Design Server APIs
use_cases.description: Plan Nitro server routes, request handlers, middleware, plugins, and shared server utilities.

use_cases.title: Choose Rendering Modes
use_cases.description: Select SSR, client rendering, prerendering, or hybrid route rules for performance and SEO goals.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Nuxt Structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the key folders in my Nuxt app and when to use pages, components, composables, server, and plugins.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Data Fetching
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Nuxt data fetching approach. Recommend when to use useFetch, useAsyncData, $fetch, lazy fetching, and refresh.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Server Routes
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Nuxt server API for this feature. Include routes, middleware, validation, error handling, and where shared utilities should live.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Rendering Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this Nuxt rendering strategy. Compare SSR, CSR, prerendering, route rules, hydration risk, caching, and deployment tradeoffs.

output_examples.input: How should I fetch product data for an SSR product page?
output: Use useFetch for data needed during initial render and SEO indexing.
Add a stable key when multiple calls can share cached data.
Use lazy fetching only for non-critical sections below the main content.

output_examples.input: Why does my composable fail outside setup?
output_examples.output: The answer explains valid Nuxt composable contexts, why module-level calls fail, and how to move runtime config access inside a function.

output_examples.input: Should this route be prerendered or server rendered?
output_examples.output: The answer compares content freshness, user-specific data, SEO needs, cache behavior, and route rule options.

best_practices: Share the Nuxt version, deployment target, and current file structure when asking for architecture help.
Ask for SSR, hydration, and security tradeoffs when designing data or server routes.
Validate generated guidance against your project modules, runtime config, and production hosting rules.
anti_patterns: Do not use $fetch alone in setup for initial SSR data because it can fetch twice.
Do not store request-specific state at module scope in server-rendered code.
Do not expose private runtime config or secrets through public client code.

faq.question: What Nuxt version does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It focuses on Nuxt 3.x reference material generated on January 28, 2026.

faq.question: Can it help with Nuxt routing?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers file-based routes, dynamic parameters, navigation, middleware, layouts, and validation.

faq.question: Does it execute Nuxt commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance. Command execution depends on the host AI tool and user approval.

faq.question: Can it help with server routes?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains Nitro handlers, middleware, plugins, event context, streaming, and error handling.

faq.question: Does it include deployment advice?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Nitro output, Node deployment patterns, and platform-focused deployment considerations.

faq.question: Can it replace the official Nuxt documentation?
faq.answer: No. It is a focused assistant reference and should be checked against official docs for new releases.
